strings.why.disclaimer: Benchmarks are general rules of thumb from the sources named. They are not financial advice and vary by country and situation.
strings.why.basis.avg: Average of your last {n} completed period(s)
strings.why.assumedNet: No gross income is set in Settings, so your recorded income (usually after tax) is used. Lenders use gross income, so this ratio reads higher than theirs.
strings.why.rule.none: Add some income and spending to see this.
strings.why.forecast.f:
Expected daily spending = your everyday spending after removing one-off purchases (now {daily} a day; a typical week is {week}).
Projected balance = today's cash + scheduled bills and income − expected spending.
The shaded band is the 80% range: expected spending ± 1.28 × your usual spread, growing with √days.
strings.why.health.f: Score out of 100 = savings rate (30) + budget discipline (25) + emergency fund (25) + debt load (20).
strings.why.xirr.f: Find the yearly rate r where the sum of cash flow ÷ (1 + r)^(days since the first flow ÷ 365) equals zero. Money you put in counts negative; money you take out, and today's value, count positive.
strings.why.loan.f:
Monthly interest = balance × APR ÷ 12.
Payment for a term = balance × i ÷ (1 − (1 + i)^−months), where i = APR ÷ 12.
Each month interest is paid first; the rest of the payment reduces the balance.
strings.why.recurring.f: A payee is suggested when it repeats on a steady rhythm (weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly, quarterly or yearly) at least 3 times (2 for yearly), the gaps agree within a few days, and the amounts stay within about 35% of their median.
strings.why.networth.n: Foreign-currency accounts are converted with the exchange rates you typed in Settings. Penny also saves a snapshot every day, so the history chart shows real past values from now on.
strings.why.rule.n: Needs = categories marked Need (by default groceries, housing, utilities, transport, health, education); wants = everything else. Change a category's type when you edit it.
strings.why.dti.n: Counts the monthly payment you entered on each loan or credit account.
strings.why.forecast.n1: One-off purchases far above your usual amounts are left out of the daily estimate so one big buy does not distort the future. They are listed above.
strings.why.forecast.n2: With under 28 days of history the range is wide and confidence is low. Weekday patterns need 8+ weeks; yearly seasonality needs 13+ months.
strings.why.forecast.n3: This is a projection from your own history, not a prediction or advice.
strings.why.health.n: The score is a summary for orientation only.
strings.why.xirr.n: Dividends and fees recorded on the account are part of the return; transfers in and out are the cash flows.
strings.why.xirr.short: Under 3 months of history: an annualised figure can be misleading.
strings.why.loan.n: Interest is rounded to the cent each month, like a lender's statement. Your lender's figures may differ slightly.
strings.why.recurring.n: Suggestions are never created automatically. You choose which ones to track.
strings.why.savings.b: Saving at least 20% of income is a common target.
strings.why.savings.s: 50/30/20 budgeting rule — Elizabeth Warren & Amelia Warren Tyagi, “All Your Worth” (2005)
strings.why.rule.b: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt repayment.
strings.why.rule.s: Elizabeth Warren & Amelia Warren Tyagi, “All Your Worth” (2005)
strings.why.emergency.b: Planners commonly suggest 3 to 6 months of essential expenses in cash. Penny uses 6 as the goal; one-income or irregular-pay households often aim for the high end.
strings.why.emergency.s: Common financial-planning guidance (a rule of thumb, not a regulation)
strings.why.dti.b: 36% or less of gross income going to all debt payments.
strings.why.dti.s: The traditional 28/36 lender guideline (a mortgage-underwriting rule of thumb; limits vary by lender and country)
strings.why.housing.b: 28% or less of gross income going to housing.
strings.why.housing.s: The traditional 28/36 lender guideline (a mortgage-underwriting rule of thumb; limits vary by lender and country)

strings.about.legalEn: The English text is the binding version.
strings.help.title: Help
strings.help.b.start: Add your accounts first (Accounts → New), then log spending with N or the + button. Penny works out balances, budgets and forecasts from what you enter.
strings.help.b.accounts: Each account has its own currency. Totals are converted into your main currency with the exchange rates you type in Settings → Language & money. If a rate is missing, Penny says so instead of guessing.
strings.help.b.tx: Use Split on the Add sheet to divide one receipt across categories; the parts must add up to the total. Penny asks before saving a date in the future or a likely duplicate.
strings.help.b.import: Transactions → Import accepts CSV, TSV, OFX and QFX. Check the columns and date order in the preview, skip duplicates, and use Undo if anything looks wrong. A safety backup is taken first.
strings.help.b.budgets: Set a monthly limit per category. Turn on carry-over to roll unspent money (or overspending) into the next month.
strings.help.b.health: Savings rate, 50/30/20, emergency fund, debt-to-income and housing ratio are measured over your last completed months. Tap the ? beside any number to see the formula, your inputs and the benchmark.
strings.help.b.forecast: The forecast uses your typical spending (the median, not the average), ignores one-off outliers, and shows an 80% range. It gets more reliable with more months of data.
strings.help.b.recurring: Penny finds repeating payments in your history and offers to turn them into bills. Bills and reminders can post automatically.
strings.help.b.backup: Penny keeps automatic backups. To move to a new PC, export a copy from Settings → Data & backups and import it there.
strings.help.b.privacy: Your data is one file on this PC and is never uploaded. The passcode is a privacy screen, not encryption; use Windows disk encryption for stronger protection.
strings.help.b.trouble: Every bulk change and import has an Undo. You can restore any automatic backup from Settings → Data & backups, and open the log folder to share with support.
